messages.author: 5c24954f6be9e2ef
messages.subject: Sampling freezes at the 2nd chain.
parts:
I have tried for several times since yesterday but the sampling stops at the 2nd chain each time. The code is below and stan files are attached. Hopefully someone can reproduce the phenomenon.

An unrelated question, to avoid recompiling the model, do we always need to first run fit <- stan() and then pass fit to stan for more iterations and chains? Or there is anyway to save the compiled model and load it later? Can anyone give me a link that I can follow?

```{r}
library(rstan)
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
n <- 4 ## number of layers
N <- n+1 ## Number of yhats
theta <- c(kpwa = log(2)/100, kpse = log(2)/100, Kd = 50)
Zs <- 2
Zsed <- rep(Zs/n,n)
x_r <- c(rhob=2.05,theta=0.5,Zw=5,Dp=0.05,delta=1,Zsed)
fixpar <- x_r
y0 <- c(1,rep(0,n))
ts <- seq(1,100,by=10)
T <- length(ts)
t0 <- 0.0
## sm <- stan_model(file="WS4.stan")
swData <- stan(file="RPest/stan/WS4.stan",data=c("T","y0","t0","ts","theta","fixpar"),chains=1,iter=1,algorithm="Fixed_param")
y <- extract(swData,"y_hat")
ypred <- y$y_hat[1,,]
y <- cbind(ypred[,1],apply(ypred[,2:N],1,sum))
```


### Direct Optimization


```{r}
fit <- stan(file="WS4fit.stan",data=c("T","y","t0","ts","theta","fixpar","N"),chains=1,iter=1)
res <- optimizing(get_stanmodel(fit), data=c("T","y","t0","ts","theta","fixpar","N"),  hessian = TRUE)
res$par[c("M0","theta[1]","theta[2]","theta[3]")]
theta
sqrt(diag(solve(-res$hessian)))

```

### MCMC Sampling

```{r}

fit2 <- stan(fit=fit,data=c("T","y","t0","ts","theta","fixpar","N"),chains=3,iter=1000)
save(fit2,file="fit2.Rdata")
print(fit2)
plot(fit2)
```

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Sampling freezes at the 2nd chain.
parts:
Does it just hang? If so, I'm guessing what happens is that you
are getting into a stiff part of the ODE parameter space, which
Stan can't handle. We have some patches in place undergoing testing
right now that should solve this problem partially for Stan 2.9 (a
few months out). And then after that, we should have a stiff ODE
solver in place for Stan 2.10 early next year.

Until then, I don't have many suggestions other than to

1. try initializing with reasonable values,

2. try setting stepsize lower so you're less likely to step into
bad parameter values early on

3. set target acceptance (adapt_delta) higher so you keep the
step size low and avoid getting into stiff regions later.

- Bob
